messages:
james: Hey team — after we bumped to @redwood/sdk 1.4.0 several of our servers started POSTing duplicate webhook deliveries when the SDK retried. We surface duplicate idempotency keys downstream. Repro attached.

support-bot: Ticket created: #INC-9843. Assigning to on-call.

maria: Sorry to hear that. Can you paste the SDK + Node + undici versions, and a minimal request sample? Also are you using a streaming body or a string/buffer?

james: Versions: Node v18.16.0, @redwood/sdk 1.4.0, undici 5.15.3. Not using streaming intentionally — we send JSON but the app uses a helper that creates a Readable from a payload in some code paths. Minimal sample (simplified):
```js
// simplified helper that we ship in prod
const controller = new AbortController();
function send(payload) {
  const stream = Readable.from([JSON.stringify(payload)]); // sometimes used
  return fetch(API_URL, { method: 'POST', body: stream, signal: controller.signal, headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' } });
}
// SDK call wraps this with a retry loop
await client.request(...);
```
We saw two actual HTTP posts for one logical call when the first attempt timed out.

omar: Hmm — two likely causes: 1) the retry wrapper reuses the same body stream or AbortController across attempts, or 2) undici/Node is replaying the body unexpectedly. Quick check: can you reproduce with a plain string body (no Readable)? If that stops duplicates it points to body/stream reuse.

james: I tried swapping to `body: JSON.stringify(payload)` and duplicates stopped. Repro only happens when we pass a Readable. Logs (timestamps redacted):
```
[info] request start id=rc1 attempt=1 body=readable
[warn] request timeout id=rc1 attempt=1 aborting
[info] retrying id=rc1 attempt=2 body=readable
[info] request start id=rc1 attempt=2 body=readable
[info] delivered webhook id=wq-45 status=200
[info] delivered webhook id=wq-45 status=200  <-- duplicate
```

ashley: That log pattern is consistent with re-using a non-rewindable stream. Fetch/undici can't re-read the same Readable once consumed, but some code paths will try to re-send it and either fail or produce duplicate semantics if the underlying socket was left open. Two followups: (A) can you ensure the SDK creates a fresh body per attempt, or buffer the body ahead of retries, (B) make a new AbortController per attempt (don't reuse).

omar: Agreed. Short-term workaround for you: convert to a buffer/string before the SDK call (as you tested). Longer-term we'll patch the SDK to detect stream-like bodies and buffer them or refuse automatic retries.

ashley: Can you also share the exact SDK client config (retry settings) so we can reproduce the retry timing/backoff?

james: config: { retries: 3, backoffMs: 500, maxBackoffMs: 3000, retryOnTimeout: true } — default client setup.

omar: Thanks. We reproduced locally with a Readable and a test server that ACKs on the second connection. Root cause: SDK retry wrapper reused the same Readable and the same AbortController instance across attempts. When the first socket timed out the SDK signaled abort, but the underlying Readable remained readable and got reconsumed by a new connection in some Node/undici timing, causing duplicate downstream deliveries.

eng-qa: We've opened PR #2842 to address two things: 1) SDK will now buffer non-file Readable bodies up to a configurable cap (default 256KB) so retries can re-send safely, and 2) we create a fresh AbortController per attempt. The PR includes a test that simulates a half-way consumed stream + retry and asserts only one delivery.

james: Nice. Any ETA for a patch we can pick up? We have customer impact.

omar: We're targeting a patch release v1.4.1 today. Workaround until then: 1) convert body to string/buffer before calling client.request, or 2) set env var REDWOOD_DISABLE_AUTO_RETRIES=true to force no automatic retries at the SDK layer.

eng-qa: Patch published: `npm i @redwood/sdk@1.4.1` — changes: buffered request bodies for retries, new config `clientConfig.retry.bufferBodyBytes`, and safe AbortController-per-attempt. Please test the patch and report back.

james: Installed 1.4.1, ran the failing job over the same traffic. No duplicate deliveries in 2k requests. Thank you :tada: 

ashley: We'll follow up with a small blog note in the changelog and a guidance doc about avoiding streaming bodies when you rely on automatic retries.

support-bot: INC-9843 marked resolved after user confirmation.

james: Appreciate the quick turnaround. Left a :heart: reaction on the PR.
